newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil up sharply at close, meal sets highs.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil up sharply at close, meal sets highs.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed strongly higher, nearly one half the daily trading limit, with late fund buying, strong soybeans and unwinding of meal/oil spreads boosting prices, traders said.
"Funds bought it late and ran it through buy stops," a trader said.
Griffin Trading and Rosenthal Collins each bought 300 December soyoil, they said. Term Commodities bought 600 December, they said.
Refco Inc did 200 Dec oil/meal and Rand Financial did 100 Dec oil/meal, they said.
New contract highs were set early in soymeal with the new high in September at $275.80 per ton, up from the previous high of $274.50 set Wednesday.
The soy complex was boosted by some forecasts for frost in key areas of the U.S. Midwest as early as September 21.
Soyoil closed 0.30 to 0.51 cent per lb higher, with September up 0.50 at 25.89. Soymeal was unchanged to $2.30 per ton higher, with September up $2.10 at $275.60.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 25,000, down from 28,826 Wednesday, according to the CBOT. Soymeal options volume was estimated at 3,000, up from 2,433 Wednesday.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 26,000 contracts, down from 31,729 Wednesday. Soyoil options volume was estimated at 4,500 contracts, up from 1,190 Wednesday.
